question.knowledge_point: Finding a Scalar Factor When Direction Reverses
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931259/assets/551316d1e36175ca302c5c472d4109a9bc9cadf32cc85d2a1751424a386070cc.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a-2b,$ find $\lambda .$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a-2b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $-2b.$ So, we first draw the vector $-2b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931259/assets/40a0137d6227212db9b7ef9f349029838f3f51398790ec5e1c304e12c3743a0f.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $-2b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=\frac{1}{2}|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-\frac{1}{2}a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =-2b-\frac{1}{2}a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a-2b=-\frac{1}{2}a-2b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-\frac{1}{2}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Expressing a Vector That Satisfies a Ratio in Terms of Known Vectors
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931259/assets/040127594f639248736d4492f1853bcb1e6ef18c37db9242ebe466045713628a.png)

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OU}=u,$ $\overset{\to }{OV}=v$ and $W$ divides $\overset{―}{UV}$ in the ratio $UW:WV=2:7.$ Find $\overset{\to }{OW}.$
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OW}=\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{UW}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OU}=u,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{UW}.$

First, from $△OUV,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{UV} & =\overset{\to }{UO}+\overset{\to }{OV} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{OV} \\  & =-u+v \\  & =v-u.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $UW:WV=2:7,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{UW}=\frac{2}{9}\overset{\to }{UV}=\frac{2}{9}(v-u).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OW} & =\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{UW} \\  & =u+\frac{2}{9}(v-u) \\  & =\frac{7}{9}u+\frac{2}{9}v.\end{aligned}
$$
